title: Aged care algorithms need redesign, human override, inquiry finds
headline: Aged care algorithms need redesign and human override, Senate finds
summary: A year-long Senate inquiry has concluded that automated decision-making algorithms used in aged care must be fundamentally redesigned. The inquiry calls for new human overrides at the point of assessment to address inaccurate and inappropriate care level decisions.
why_it_matters: Organisations deploying automated decision systems in regulated care sectors face heightened pressure to implement robust human-in-the-loop safeguards and system redesigns.

quotes.text: Aged care algorithms making inaccurate and inappropriate automated decisions on care levels must be “fundamentally” redesigned and safeguarded by new human overrides at the point of assessment, a year-long Senate inquiry has found.

The findings add pressure on the Albanese government to overhaul the so-called Integrated Assessment Tool, which is already under review and has been widely criticised by the Ombudsman, state governments and aged care experts.

dates_mentioned.what: Publication date of the Senate inquiry findings report

classification.significance_reason: A parliamentary inquiry finding significant flaws in a national government automated assessment tool highlights critical public sector AI governance and oversight requirements.
